title: Second-Order Minimax Risk for Treatment Effects under Asymmetric Outcome Bounds

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery audited the original unrestricted fixed-positive 2:1 finite-population ATE problem and strengthened its matching sharp leading and Airy correction to every fixed positive cap ratio, preserving dependent assignments, retained seeds, labels and the realized target. Mathematics, cited-source verification and decision review passed, but the cold paper-score ceiling 7.2 fell below the field gate 7.4, and independent main validity found no bounded same-topic tier repair. Arbitrary intermediate count-law tails and exact finite optimality remain open; F stages never ran, no Lean theorem was verified, and no substrate was promoted.
tldr: For every fixed positive treatment cap \(\lambda\) and unit control cap, the unrestricted fixed-table causal risk is \(R_n(\lambda)=\lambda/n-\{\lambda^2(\lambda+1)^2\}^{1/3}|\alpha|n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), uniformly on compact positive cap intervals. Outcome-blind Bernoulli allocation \(\lambda/(\lambda+1)\), a baseline-aware nonlinear action and its original-record polynomial extension attain both terms. A conditional-target converse retains missing potential-outcome variance against every assignment law and analysis. The equal-cap boundary recovers the published common-support finite value. Compact-interior and negligible-tail count laws have a complete second-order characterization; arbitrary intermediate tails remain open.
gap: The common-support unrestricted theorem uses a target-preserving symmetry that fails after unequal arm normalization. Heterogeneous rectangular-total results restrict analysis to design-unbiased estimators. Neither comparison identifies the original all-procedure sharp correction.
fill: Retain the four-response-type experiment and construct a conditional-target information bound before deriving the limiting risk operator. Match a uniform full-record upper to a complete-table all-design lower, then characterize sharp-optimal count laws.
